name: Stats

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.code:
<>
  <Title as="h2" textSize="5" id="stats-kpis">
    This month
  </Title>
  <Stats aria-labelledby="stats-kpis" minCol={8} gap={4}>
    <Stat
      label="Revenue"
      value={8456.4}
      format={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }}
      locale="en-US"
      change={0.12}
      description="since last month"
    />
    <Stat
      label="New customers"
      value={1234}
      locale="en-US"
      change={-0.019}
      description="since last month"
    />
    <Stat
      label="Churn"
      value={0.021}
      format={{ style: 'percent', maximumFractionDigits: 1 }}
      locale="en-US"
      change={0.004}
      changeColor="danger"
      description="since last month"
    />
    <Stat
      label="Requests"
      value={1234567}
      format={{ notation: 'compact' }}
      locale="en-US"
      change={0}
      description="since last month"
    />
  </Stats>
</>

examples.title: Tile Width and Gap
examples.code:
<Stats minCol={5} gap={2}>
  <Stat label="Mon" value={12} />
  <Stat label="Tue" value={18} />
  <Stat label="Wed" value={9} />
  <Stat label="Thu" value={21} />
  <Stat label="Fri" value={15} />
</Stats>

examples.title: Text Color
examples.code:
<Stats minCol={8} textColor="link">
  <Stat label="Revenue" value="$8,456" />
  <Stat label="Refunds" value="$312" textColor="danger" />
</Stats>

examples.title: In a LocaleProvider
examples.code:
<LocaleProvider locale="de-DE">
  <Stats minCol={8} gap={4}>
    <Stat
      label="Umsatz"
      value={8456.4}
      format={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' }}
      change={-0.019}
    />
    <Stat label="Neukunden" value={1234} change={0.12} />
  </Stats>
</LocaleProvider>

examples.title: Compound (dot-notation) usage
examples.code:
<Stats minCol={8} gap={4}>
  <Stats.Stat label="Revenue" value="$8,456" description="this month" />
  <Stats.Stat>
    <Stats.Stat.Label>New customers</Stats.Stat.Label>
    <Stats.Stat.Value>1,234</Stats.Stat.Value>
    <Stats.Stat.Description>this month</Stats.Stat.Description>
  </Stats.Stat>
</Stats>

accessibility:
- **One list for the row:** a `<dl>` with a `<div>` for each Stat, which browsers expose as a list
  of terms and their definitions. Chromium, Firefox and WebKit give the same tree: each label
  followed by its figure, its change and its note, in the order written.
- **A name from the heading above:** point `aria-labelledby` at it, as in
  [Basic Usage](https://bestax.io/docs/api/elements/stats#basic-usage).
- **Only Stats inside:** a `<dl>` holds only its groups, so put nothing else in the row, and wrap
  no Stat in it. A `LocaleProvider` or a `Box` goes around the whole row instead. A
  `role="status"` element doesn't: it goes around one lone Stat whose figure should be announced,
  since announcing a whole row that refreshes would be noise.
- **Reading order is the order you write:** the grid places the tiles and follows the writing
  direction, so in a right-to-left page the first tile sits on the right, and a screen reader
  reads them in the same order either way.
- **Not interactive and not live:** it has no tab stop and announces nothing when a figure
  changes. See [`Stat`](https://bestax.io/docs/api/elements/stat#a-figure-that-should-be-announced) for the one figure that
  should be announced.
summary: The `Stats` component lays out a row of `Stat`s, such as the key figures at the top of a dashboard, as one description list on Bulma's smart grid. It's a `<dl>` with a `<div>` for each Stat, so a screen reader announces the row once, then each label with its values. The tiles fill the grid's columns, each at least `minCol` wide, and wrap without media queries; the `gap` helper prop sets the space between them. Name the row with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the heading above it. `Stat` is also `Stats.Stat`.

props.name: children
props.description: `Stat`s, one per figure, and nothing else: they're the groups of its `<dl>`.

props.name: minCol
props.description: The narrowest a tile gets before the row wraps (`is-col-min-*`), as Grid's `minCol`: 1.5rem a step. Unset, it's Bulma's 9rem.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color helper: `has-text-*` on the `<dl>`, as on Buttons. Each Stat in the row without a `textColor` of its own takes it too, which colors its figure, since a Stat sets its own color. The labels, the changes and the notes keep theirs.

extraProps.name: gap
extraProps.description: The space between tiles (`is-gap-*`), the helper prop with the values Grid's `gap` takes.

extraProps.name: aria-labelledby
extraProps.description: The id of the heading above the row, which names it.

parts.summary: The `Stat` component shows a figure with its name, and often a change and a note, such as a dashboard's revenue or an account's storage used. It's a label and its values in a description list: a `<dt>` for the label, and a `<dd>` each for the figure, the change and the note. On its own it renders its own `<dl>`; inside `Stats` it's a `<div>` in the row's. A number `value` is written by `NumberFormatter`, so it follows a `LocaleProvider`. A change is written with its sign ("+12%"), so the direction is in the text, beside a decorative arrow and a color.

props.name: label
props.description: What the figure is ("Revenue"), as a `Stat.Label` before the children. A Stat needs one, here or as a `Stat.Label` child: it's the figure's name for assistive tech, and a definition list's values belong to a term. A Stat with neither a `label` nor a `Stat.Label` child warns in development.

props.name: value
props.description: The figure, as a `Stat.Value` after the children. A number is written by `NumberFormatter` with `format` and `locale`; anything else, such as "N/A", renders as given, and `0` renders. `undefined`, `null`, a boolean and `''` leave it empty, and its `<dd>` still renders, one line of the figure tall, while the Stat has a label, so the label keeps its definition while the figure is missing. A `Stat.Value` child takes its place: with one, `value` and its `<dd>` are left out.

props.name: format
props.description: `Intl.NumberFormat` options for a number `value`, as NumberFormatter's `format`. A `value` that isn't a number ignores it.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale for `value` and `change`, as NumberFormatter's `locale`. Unset, it's the `LocaleProvider`'s around it, and with neither, the runtime's own, so give one, here or through a `LocaleProvider`, on a page rendered on the server.

props.name: change
props.description: The change, as a `Stat.Change` after the value. With the default format it's a fraction (`0.12` for 12%); with your own `changeFormat`, it's in that format's terms. It's written with its sign, so the direction is in the text.

props.name: changeFormat
props.description: `Intl.NumberFormat` options for `change`. Yours replace the default, and `signDisplay: 'exceptZero'` is added unless you set a `signDisplay`. With `signDisplay: 'never'`, or `'negative'` on a rise, the text carries no direction: the arrow is hidden from assistive tech and the tone is color alone, so keep a sign, or say the direction in `description`.

props.name: changeColor
props.description: The change's color. Unset, it's the sign's: `success` up, `danger` down, and none at zero. Set it where up is bad news, such as a cost or an error rate.

props.name: description
props.description: A note under the figure ("since last month"), as a `Stat.Description` last.

props.name: size
props.description: The figure's size, a step of Bulma's size scale. The label, the change and the note stay small.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a `Skeleton` in place of `value`, one line of the figure tall, and sets `aria-busy` on the Stat. The label, the change and the note render as given. With a `Stat.Value` child, it only sets `aria-busy`: the child renders as given, so put a `Skeleton` in it yourself.

props.name: children
props.description: `Stat.Label`, `Stat.Value`, `Stat.Change` and `Stat.Description`, for anything the props don't cover, such as a unit or an info tip. They render between `label` and `value`. They're this Stat's own parts, so not another Stat: that would be a list inside this one's. The Stat finds a `Stat.Label` or `Stat.Value` among them by type, so one rendered from inside a component of your own isn't seen.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color helper. It colors the figure; the label, the change and the note keep their own colors. Inside `Stats`, a Stat without one takes the row's.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the root, a `<div>` inside `Stats` or a `<dl>` on its own.
